title: Be the preprocessor
description:
The preprocessor's `#define` is plain text substitution. Write `expand(line, defines)` to do the same job for simple object-like macros.

`defines` maps macro names to their replacement text. Replace every **whole word** in `line` that is a macro name with its replacement. A word is a run of letters, digits and underscores. Everything else in the line is copied unchanged.

```
defines: MAX_HEALTH -> 100, BONUS -> 25
expand("hp = MAX_HEALTH + BONUS;")       gives  "hp = 100 + 25;"
expand("MAX_HEALTH_BAR = 3;")            gives  "MAX_HEALTH_BAR = 3;"   (a different word)
```

One pass is enough: the replacement text is not itself expanded again.
hints: Walk along the line with an index. When the character is not part of a word, copy it to the output and move on. A word character is a letter, a digit or `_`: compare against the ranges `'a'` to `'z'`, `'A'` to `'Z'` and `'0'` to `'9'`, or use `std::isalnum(static_cast<unsigned char>(c))` from `<cctype>`, which is true for letters and digits.
When it is part of a word, keep moving until the word ends, then take that whole word with `substr`. Look it up in the map with `find`.

A `std::map` holds key and value pairs. `defines.find(word)` returns an iterator: either `defines.end()`, meaning the key is not there, or a pointer-like handle to the pair, whose `->first` is the key and `->second` the value.

```cpp
const auto found{ defines.find(word) };
if (found != defines.end()) out += found->second;   // a macro: use its replacement
```

If `find` returns `end()`, the word is not a macro: copy the word itself.
lessonTitle: How Source Code Becomes Machine Code
